The [score function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-score) is vector-valued; 
its components are:

$$
\derivf{\llik}{\vb} 
= \pmat{
\derivf{\llik}{\b_0}
\\
\derivf{\llik}{\b_1}
\\
\vdots
\\
\derivf{\llik}{\b_p}
}
= \pmat{
\sumin 1 \eps_i
\\
\sumin x_{i,1}\eps_i
\\
\vdots
\\
\sumin x_{i,p} \eps_i
}
= \pmat{
\v1 \cdot \veps
\\
\mX_{\cdot 1} \cdot \veps
\\
\vdots
\\
\mX_{\cdot p} \cdot \veps}
$$

Here, $\mX_{\cdot j} \eqdef (x_{1j}, \ldots, x_{nj})$ denotes
the $j^{th}$ column of the [design matrix](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-projections.html#def-design-matrix) $\mX$
(the $n$-vector of covariate $j$'s values across all observations),
in contrast with $\vx_i$,
which denotes observation $i$'s covariate row vector (a $p$-vector).

Thus, the [score equation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-score-equation) $\vec{\llik'} = \mathbf{0}_{(p+1) \times 1}$ means that
for the [MLE](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-mle) $\evb$:

1. the sum of the errors (aka deviations) equals 0:

$$\sumin \eps_i = 0$$

2. the sums of the errors times each covariate also equal 0:

$$\mX_{\cdot j} \cdot \veps = \sumin x_{ij} \eps_i = 0, \forall j \in \set{1:p}$$
